event_overview.title: About Russia-Ukraine War
event_overview.subject: Russia-Ukraine War
event_overview.summary: The Russia-Ukraine War is an ongoing armed conflict between Ukraine and the Russian Federation, rooted in fighting that began in eastern Ukraine in 2014 and greatly escalated with Russia’s full-scale invasion on February 24, 2022. It has involved conventional ground operations as well as long-range missile and drone attacks, and has produced a major humanitarian and displacement crisis.

facts.label: Origins and escalation
facts.value: Conflict-related humanitarian operations in eastern Ukraine expanded in 2014; Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022 transformed the conflict into a nationwide emergency.

facts.label: Main parties and geography
facts.value: The war principally involves Ukraine and the Russian Federation, with military operations taking place in Ukraine and attacks increasingly affecting areas beyond the immediate front line.

facts.label: International legal position
facts.value: On March 2, 2022, the UN General Assembly deplored Russia’s aggression against Ukraine, demanded that Russia end its use of force and withdraw its forces, and reaffirmed Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders.

facts.label: International Court of Justice proceedin
facts.value: In provisional measures issued on March 16, 2022 in Ukraine v. Russian Federation, the International Court of Justice ordered Russia to suspend military operations begun on February 24, 2022, while stating that the order did not decide the case’s merits.

facts.label: Humanitarian impact
facts.value: The war has driven large-scale displacement, damaged civilian infrastructure and left millions of people in need of assistance; UNHCR describes it as an ongoing full-scale war and humanitarian emergency.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline focuses on specified late-July and early-August 2026 security developments, including cross-border drone or missile incidents and strikes; it does not aim to provide a complete account of the war’s military, diplomatic, legal, or humanitarian history.

event_overview.title: About Typhoon Dolphin
event_overview.subject: Typhoon Dolphin
event_overview.summary: Typhoon Dolphin was the 13th named tropical cyclone of the 2026 western North Pacific season, forming in late July and later tracking westward across the region. It affected Japan’s Okinawa area before making landfall in Zhejiang province on China’s east coast; by August 10 it had weakened to a tropical storm inland.

facts.value: China’s National Meteorological Center designated Dolphin as 2026’s No. 13 typhoon; official reporting said it formed over the northwestern Pacific on July 27, 2026.

facts.value: Dolphin made landfall near Taizhou, Zhejiang, on the evening of August 9 with reported winds of 151 kph; on August 10, China’s National Meteorological Center listed it as a tropical storm over Dexing, Jiangxi, and forecast further weakening.

facts.label: Naming system
facts.value: “Dolphin” is a name contributed by Hong Kong, China, under the ESCAP/WMO Typhoon Committee naming list; it refers to the Chinese white dolphin and a Hong Kong mascot.

event_overview.title: About Crime Extradition
event_overview.subject: Crime Extradition
event_overview.summary: This event concerns the transfer of Irish national Daniel Kinahan from the United Arab Emirates to Ireland under the two countries’ extradition framework, so that he can face criminal proceedings in Ireland. Reporting on the transfer said he was expected to appear before Ireland’s Special Criminal Court on an allegation of directing an organized crime group; the allegation remains to be determined through the Irish judicial process.

facts.label: Extradition framework
facts.value: Ireland and the UAE concluded their bilateral extradition treaty in Abu Dhabi on October 21, 2024. Ireland’s Extradition (United Arab Emirates) Order 2025 brought the UAE within Part II of Ireland’s Extradition Act 1965 from May 18, 2025.

facts.label: Legal scope
facts.value: Under the treaty, either state may seek a person for prosecution, trial, or execution of a sentence. For a prosecution request, the conduct must be punishable in both states by at least one year of imprisonment.

facts.label: Responsible authorities
facts.value: The treaty names Ireland’s Minister for Justice, or departmental officials exercising the minister’s functions, as Ireland’s central authority; the UAE Ministry of Justice is the UAE central authority.

facts.label: Broader enforcement context
facts.value: In April 2022, the U.S. Treasury Department designated the Kinahan Organized Crime Group and Daniel Kinahan under its transnational-crime sanctions authority; sanctions are an administrative measure and separate from the Irish criminal case.

event_overview.title: About Typhoon Dolphin
event_overview.subject: Typhoon Dolphin
event_overview.summary: Typhoon Dolphin was the 13th named tropical cyclone of the 2026 western North Pacific season, forming in late July and later tracking westward across the region. It affected Japan’s Okinawa area before making landfall in Zhejiang province on China’s east coast; by August 10 it had weakened to a tropical storm inland.

facts.label: Formation and designation
facts.value: China’s National Meteorological Center designated Dolphin as 2026’s No. 13 typhoon; official reporting said it formed over the northwestern Pacific on July 27, 2026.

facts.label: China landfall and weakening
facts.value: Dolphin made landfall near Taizhou, Zhejiang, on the evening of August 9 with reported winds of 151 kph; on August 10, China’s National Meteorological Center listed it as a tropical storm over Dexing, Jiangxi, and forecast further weakening.

facts.label: Naming system
facts.value: “Dolphin” is a name contributed by Hong Kong, China, under the ESCAP/WMO Typhoon Committee naming list; it refers to the Chinese white dolphin and a Hong Kong mascot.

items.text: A Ukrainian drone attack on the industrial city of Nizhnekamsk in Tatarstan has resulted in at least 13 fatalities and numerous injuries.
